text:
Maria: Heads up—Support opened a Sev2. Multiple customers started getting 401s after today's cross-SDK regen. Repro steps attached below.
Emma: Ticket #2456 — ~120 401 responses in last hour, mostly from newly published SDKs. Also seeing retries that ballooned tokens/billing. Sample curl from customer: 
```bash
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://api.redwood.com/v1/models
```
Jon: Which SDK versions did they upgrade to? We pushed regen this morning.
Emma: Python: 0.9.4 -> 0.9.5, TS: 1.12.0 -> 1.12.1. Only the new releases show the failure; pinned older clients are fine.
Raj: Sounds like either header casing changed or auth middleware ordering shifted in the generated pipeline. In past regens a template tweak moved header injection later.
Jon: Investigating locally now. Running a quick repro with the new python client.
Jon: ```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('TOKEN'))
resp = client.models.list()
print(resp.status_code, resp.headers.get('authorization'), resp.request.headers)
```
Jon: Repro'd — outgoing request has no Authorization header on the wire for the python generated client (it's in the request object but the generator wraps/renames headers into a `headers` param and the final transport ignores it).
CI-bot: Build #198 (regen-template) passed unit tests but no auth-integration tests present. :eyes:
Maria: OK. Two simultaneous issues then: (A) header handling regression in template, (B) retry behavior in TS client causing duplicate attempts and billing. Need containment and fix plan.
Raj: On the TS side I saw the retry middleware now retries on 401; that's wrong — 401 should be auth-failure (no retry). That explains the billing spike.
Emma: Billing ops reports a customer billed ~2.6x because client retried 2 extra times on 401. They're asking for a refund while we fix.
Jon: Plan: 1) revert/patch the header emission in the python/ts templates so Authorization is always set at transport-layer time, 2) change retry policy to treat 401/403 as terminal errors, 3) publish patched minor releases, 4) add an integration test to regen CI to exercise auth header roundtrip.
Maria: +1. Also add a changelog entry and mention the regen CI test requirement in the PR template. We need to avoid silent regressions.
Jon: Opening PR with fixes and tests: https://github.com/redwood/clients/pull/321 — includes python fix, ts fix, and a small integration harness that runs against local api-mock.
SRE-Oncall: Before publishing, can we gate global rollout with a short client-side toggle? If not, at least push patched packages to npm/pypi and coordinate with support to throttle customers.
Jon: Publishing now: python 0.9.6, ts 1.12.2. Also added CI test that will fail future regen if auth header is dropped.
Emma: Support confirmed with customer: auth accepted, 401 gone after they upgraded to the patched versions. Billing ops processed credit for duplicate charges.
Maria: Great work — please follow up with a short postmortem in #postmortems and update the regen checklist to include auth integration test and changelog requirement.
Emma: Closing ticket #2456 after confirmation. Thanks team.
